claims.claim: St. Brendan's Hospital ethics committee has three voting members: Dr. Helen Osei (chair), Dr. Raj Patel, and Sister Margaret Doyle (lay member).
The committee decides by simple majority of votes cast; the chair puts a motion and members vote in the room.
The committee meets 12 March 2026 at 2:00 PM America/New_York to consider a compassionate-use request for an unapproved oncology therapy.
Hospital pharmacist Tomas Lindqvist was asked to prepare a safety review of the therapy and circulate it to members before the meeting.
The manufacturer released updated trial safety data on 10 March 2026 at 8:00 AM America/New_York showing a lower rate of severe adverse events than previously reported.
Lindqvist monitors manufacturer bulletins as part of his role and acts on them the same working day.
A safety review of this kind takes Lindqvist roughly half a working day to prepare.
Reviews are circulated to committee members by hospital email, which delivers within about a minute.
Dr. Osei has said she will not approve compassionate use without current safety data, and considers the older adverse-event rate disqualifying.
Dr. Patel has consistently voted to approve compassionate use where a safety review is available and favourable.
Sister Doyle votes with the documented safety assessment when one has been provided to her.

Osei and Patel work at the hospital and check email several times during the working day; Doyle is off-site on retreat from 10 to 12 March and the hospital has no email contact with her during it, but she attends the meeting in person.
Members are present in the meeting room and hear motions put by the chair immediately.
Stating a vote in the room takes a moment; the chair's opening remarks and motion take about five minutes.
